decisions.statement: One page declares what each exit code is, and every other file imports it.
A code is judged where the answer carries refusals, whether an object spells it or a call hands it.
A refusal whose code is a number rather than a name is refused.
A number that is no exit code is left alone there too.
A module building a command's answer spells the number its test reads.
A call handing a refusal builder a number where its code goes is refused.
The builders judged are the command-answering exports taking an exit code as an argument.
A code is looked for in the last argument, since each builder takes it in a place of its own.
An answer whose list of refusals is empty says nothing went wrong, and is left alone.
A list of refusals no literal spells is read as carrying them.
A builder of that name taking no code is not seen, since no number is ever handed it.
A number inside an expression is not judged, only a number written on its own.
A name is refused only where the number beside it is the one that name means.
One of those names holding another number is left alone.
A declaration inside a function is refused as one at the top of a file is.
An exported declaration is refused as a private one is.
A name read from another page rather than from a number is not seen.

definition: the rule refusing an exit code spelled as a number away from the page declaring the five
